ownerApproval.scope: codec profile defaults only; no waiver of package, security, real-app, listening, or physical C2 gates

decision.reason: The 20 ms Opus profile and deterministic WSS/QUIC budget model are credible, but only one x86_64 macOS host was benchmarked. Windows, macOS arm64, signed MSIX, signed/notarized macOS, hostile-input, real-network, and listening evidence do not exist. Current release packages contain no libopus binary, and the QUIC alternative has no integrated cross-platform package or server path.

codecProfile.decoderLossRule: For an exposed single-frame gap, decode FEC from the immediately following packet; otherwise invoke Opus PLC for exactly one scheduled frame. Never wait beyond the bounded jitter deadline.
codecProfile.selectionReason: The measured 20 ms profile uses fewer messages and less encode-plus-decode CPU per audio second than 10 ms while retaining a modeled WSS p50/p95 well below C2. DTX is disabled so press/release timing and comfort-noise behavior do not become implicit wire state.

binaryFrame.validation: Reject the whole frame before allocation when magic, version, reserved bytes, fixed profile fields, payload length, exact message length, session state, or monotonic sequence is invalid. TLS/QUIC integrity replaces an application checksum.

engineeringBaseline.security: wss only outside loopback; existing authenticated node connection
engineeringBaseline.retransmission: TCP controlled; the application never retransmits expired live frames
engineeringBaseline.headOfLine: TCP loss can delay later audio; modeled explicitly and still requires physical two-home validation
engineeringBaseline.queuePolicy: One eight-frame/160 ms queue per recipient. Drop the oldest unsent live frame on overflow and continue other recipients without waiting.

datagramAlternative.benefit: unreliable delivery exposes loss to FEC/PLC and avoids TCP stream head-of-line recovery
datagramAlternative.rejectionForThisBaseline: No coordinator, Go, Swift, Windows or package integration exists; datagram receive is disabled by default and must be negotiated; signed/notarized cross-platform native-library evidence is absent.

opusBenchmark.boundary: Synthetic signal on one macOS 15.7.4 x86_64 host; no Windows, arm64, signed package, real app, physical network, or intelligibility claim.

transportModel.boundary: Deterministic assumptions and queue behavior only; a modeled budget pass is not C2 acceptance.

supplyAndSecurity.softwareLicense: libopus reference implementation is BSD-3-Clause; binary redistribution must carry the copyright, conditions, and disclaimer.
supplyAndSecurity.patentDisposition: The Opus project publishes royalty-free grants and patent-termination conditions plus third-party IPR caveats. This record is not legal advice; preserve exact notices and re-review if implementation or markets change.
supplyAndSecurity.updateRule: Pin source hash, patches, compiler, architectures and binary hashes; rescan the exact source and binaries on every release; no runtime code download.
supplyAndSecurity.vulnerabilityDisposition: No zero-CVE claim is made. Release remains blocked until exact source and packaged binaries pass the chosen current vulnerability scanners and hostile-frame tests. CVE-2026-40614 concerns PJSIP 2.16 and earlier Opus wrapper buffer sizing, not a libopus 1.6.1 finding; it reinforces the 400-byte pre-allocation boundary.
noticesRequired: Opus patent-license terms or stable reference

windows.currentRelease: CGO_ENABLED=0 Go executable plus pulsar-capture.dll; no libopus component is staged, hashed, signed, or SBOM-listed.
windows.required: Build pinned libopus 1.6.1 for amd64 and arm64, expose a bounded ABI, run hostile-input tests, stage and hash it, sign inner binaries and MSIX, and prove AppContainer load on Windows 10 and 11.

macos.currentRelease: Swift package has no libopus target or staged nested library; no arm64 benchmark, hardened-runtime signature, or notarization receipt exists.
macos.required: Build pinned libopus 1.6.1 for supported architectures, expose a bounded Swift/C ABI, run hostile-input tests, sign nested code, retain sandbox, notarize, and prove launch from the shipped package.

quic.required: If selected later, pin MsQuic source and binary hashes, implement/benchmark both clients and coordinator, enable and negotiate datagrams, package/sign/notarize all native code, and rerun this decision.

openBlockers.block: No Windows libopus benchmark or signed MSIX load evidence.
No macOS arm64 packaged benchmark or signed/notarized load evidence.
No exact runtime SBOM, current binary vulnerability scan, hostile-frame containment, or update receipt.
No physical Windows-Windows, Windows-macOS, macOS-macOS two-home p50/p95, 2 percent loss, intelligibility, or 100-cycle evidence.

manualHandoff.requiredEvidence: Real packaged app on physical Windows/macOS hardware, two home networks, 2 percent loss/jitter/reorder/backpressure, calibrated p50/p95, agreed intelligibility method, and 100 lifecycle cycles.
